interpretation.summary: A propulsive and iconic synth-pop drum pattern built around a four-on-the-floor kick. The groove is defined by the interplay between a driving, low-end kick, a sharp backbeat snare, and a layer of syncopated, tonal percussion. Crisp 16th-note hi-hats and shakers provide a constant, high-frequency energy, creating a feel that is both metronomic and dynamic.

vocabulary.timbre: A clean, digital palette combining punchy, tonal synth drums (kick, toms) with sharp, filtered noise elements (snare, hats, shaker). The overall sound is synthesized and precise, with a notable lack of acoustic emulation, leaning into its electronic nature.
vocabulary.brightness: Moderately bright (mean centroid 3466 Hz), characterized by crisp, cutting hi-hats and the sharp attack of the snare. The brightness is balanced by the deep, resonant kick drum, creating a full-spectrum drum mix.
vocabulary.envelope: Dominated by sharp attacks and controlled, generally short decays. The kick has a quick punch, the snare a fast crack, and the hats are tight and clipped. The exception is the open hi-hat, which provides a longer sustain on the off-beats.
vocabulary.register_density: The track builds in density, starting with a sparse kick and pitched tom pattern, then layering in the full kit at 10.6s. The register is wide, from the sub-bass frequencies of the kick to the airy highs of the shaker and hats.
vocabulary.harmony_mode: Primarily rhythmic, but with a distinct melodic component from pitched toms that loosely outlines the G# minor tonality. The percussion itself becomes a melodic hook.
vocabulary.groove: An insistent, driving 88 BPM four-on-the-floor groove. The foundation is a steady kick on every beat, a strong snare backbeat on 2 and 4, and constant 16th-note subdivision from the hats and shaker, creating a feel of perpetual motion.
vocabulary.space_grit: The production is clean and focused, with minimal-to-moderate grit. Each element occupies its own space in the mix. Subtle reverb is applied to create a sense of depth without washing out the rhythmic precision, particularly on the snare and open hat.

tracks.name: Kick
tracks.pattern: A driving four-on-the-floor pattern, hitting on every quarter note.
tracks.description: The foundational pulse of the track, present from the very beginning. It's a deep, punchy synth kick with a quick decay, providing relentless forward momentum.

tracks.name: Snare
tracks.pattern: A sharp, consistent backbeat on beats 2 and 4.
tracks.description: A crisp, electronic snare sound that provides the main backbeat. It enters at 10.6s and sounds like filtered white noise with a very fast attack and short, snappy decay. Has a touch of reverb for space.

tracks.name: Pitched Toms
tracks.pattern: A syncopated, melodic 1-bar loop that functions as a central hook.
tracks.description: A set of tonal, percussive synth toms that play a memorable, syncopated rhythm. This element is present from the start and defines the track's melodic character within the drum stem.

tracks.name: Closed Hat
tracks.pattern: Constant, driving 16th notes.
tracks.description: A very crisp and tight closed hi-hat sound that enters at 10.6s, providing high-frequency energy and driving the rhythm forward with a steady 16th-note pulse.

tracks.name: Open Hat
tracks.pattern: Syncopated off-beats, typically on the '+' of each beat.
tracks.description: An open hi-hat sound with a longer decay that adds a classic disco/synth-pop feel. It enters at 10.6s and works with the closed hat to create a more complex hi-hat pattern.

tracks.name: Shaker
tracks.pattern: Constant 16th notes, adding a high-frequency texture.
tracks.description: A bright, subtle shaker sound that plays continuous 16th notes, entering at 10.6s. It sits high in the frequency spectrum, adding a layer of airy, rhythmic texture on top of the main beat.

interpretation.score_draft: SPECULATIVE STARTER: To approximate this drum arrangement in Tone.js, start with a four-on-the-floor kick using a Tone.MembraneSynth pitched low (around C1/C2) with a fast pitch decay and a punchy envelope (short attack, medium decay). For the snare, use a Tone.NoiseSynth ('white') with a tight ADSR envelope (attack < 0.01, decay ~0.1) run through a bandpass filter around 2-3kHz. The hi-hats and shaker can also be NoiseSynths, differentiated by envelope and filtering: very tight AD envelope and a sharp high-pass filter (~5kHz) for the closed hat; longer decay (~0.2s) for the open hat; and a very high-passed (~8kHz) constant 16th-note layer for the shaker. The key melodic element is the pitched tom: use a Tone.FMSynth with low-to-mid harmonicity (1.5-2.0) and modulationIndex (~8-10) to get a percussive but tonal sound. Sequence its syncopated pattern using notes from the G# minor scale (e.g., ["", "G#2", "", "G#2", "C#3", "", "", ""]). Route the snare and open hat to a shared reverb bus with a short decay time (~0.5s) for cohesion. Set the transport BPM to 88.

interpretation.summary: A melancholic and spacious indie electronic track featuring a clear, processed female lead vocal with close harmonies. The performance is syncopated and emotive, set against a backdrop of hall reverb and subtle stereo widening effects. The track is built around the interplay between the lead melody and a lower harmony part, creating a sense of intimate dialogue.

vocabulary.timbre: The vocal timbre is clear and tonal, but has a processed, slightly thin quality, lacking significant low-mid warmth. The sound is consistent with a doubled or chorused vocal, creating a smooth but not entirely natural texture.
vocabulary.brightness: Moderately bright, with a spectral centroid of 2659 Hz. The vocals have a strong presence in the upper-mid range, allowing them to cut through a mix without being harsh or sibilant.
vocabulary.envelope: The vocals have a natural dynamic envelope with a quick attack on consonants, sustained vowels, and a controlled release, often trailing into a reverb tail at the end of phrases.
vocabulary.register_density: The lead vocal sits in a mid-to-high female register (mezzo-soprano). The arrangement density varies between a single lead vocal line and two-part harmony, with the harmony typically a third below the lead.
vocabulary.harmony_mode: The song has a strong melancholic feeling, centered around a C minor tonality. The harmonies are tight and often dissonant, using minor thirds and seconds to create tension and emotional weight, despite the measured key being its relative major (D# Major).
vocabulary.groove: The vocal rhythm is syncopated against a straight 16th-note grid. The singer's phrasing pushes and pulls against the beat, creating a human, expressive feel that avoids rigid quantization.
vocabulary.space_grit: The sound is defined by a prominent hall or plate reverb that creates a sense of space and depth, particularly noticeable on the tails of phrases. A subtle chorus or stereo-doubling effect provides width. There is no audible distortion or grit.

tracks.name: Lead and Harmony Vocals
tracks.pattern: Syncopated melodic phrases using 8th and 16th notes, often featuring a main melody with a harmony line a minor or major third below. The phrases are lyrical and follow a verse-chorus structure.
tracks.description: The central element of this stem, providing the main melody and lyrics for the entire song. It enters after the intro at 44s and continues throughout. The use of two-part harmony in the chorus sections adds emotional weight and texture. The entire track is processed with significant reverb and a subtle chorus.

interpretation.score_draft: SPECULATIVE STARTER: The vocal part can be approximated with a PolySynth to handle the harmony. Use a 'fatsawtooth' oscillator with a low count (3) and narrow spread (15) to mimic doubling without sounding too synthetic. Set a vocal-like envelope: {attack: 0.05, decay: 0.2, sustain: 0.8, release: 0.5}. A lowpass filter around 3.5kHz with a slight resonance (Q=2) will tame harshness while retaining brightness. The key is the effects chain: add a Chorus with a depth of ~0.3 and a significant send (~0.45) to a large hall Reverb. For the melody, focus on C minor, using syncopated rhythms. A sample chorus phrase ('to clap our hands above') could be transcribed on a 16n grid as: ['', '', 'G3+Eb3', '', 'G3+Eb3', '', 'C4+Ab3', 'C4+Ab3', '', 'Eb4+C4', '', 'C4+Ab3', '', '', '', ''].

interpretation.summary: An evolving synth-heavy track built on a foundation of wide, sustained pads and a prominent, syncopated, and heavily driven arpeggiated lead. The piece builds in intensity by layering melodic ideas and increasing the grit and brightness of the lead synth.

vocabulary.timbre: The timbre is predominantly synthetic, featuring detuned, sawtooth-based pads with a brassy quality, contrasted by a sharp, resonant, and metallic FM-like lead synth.
vocabulary.brightness: The track is very bright, with a high spectral centroid. The lead synth is particularly piercing, using a resonant filter with a high cutoff, while the pads occupy the mid-range.
vocabulary.envelope: A mix of envelopes are used. The pads have a slow attack and long release, creating a continuous harmonic wash. The lead has a very fast, plucky attack and quick decay, emphasizing its rhythmic role.
vocabulary.register_density: The arrangement starts with mid-register pads and builds density by adding a mid-high syncopated lead, which later moves into a higher register, spanning a wide frequency range by the climax.
vocabulary.harmony_mode: The harmony is rooted in C minor, creating a melancholic and driving mood. It relies on simple, powerful chord progressions (i-v-VI) outlined by both the pads and the arpeggiated lead.
vocabulary.groove: The groove is defined by the tension between the static, long-held pad chords and the relentless, highly syncopated 16th-note pattern of the lead synth, which provides the primary rhythmic drive.
vocabulary.space_grit: The sound has significant grit, with noticeable saturation and distortion on the lead synth. This is set within a large, ambient space created by heavy reverb on the pads, while the lead remains more direct and punchy.

tracks.name: Chorus Pad
tracks.pattern: Sustained, two-bar minor chords providing the harmonic foundation.
tracks.description: A wide, atmospheric pad that establishes the harmony from the beginning. It's characterized by its detuned, chorus-heavy sound and sits in the mid-register, creating a continuous sonic bed.

tracks.name: Driven Arp Lead
tracks.pattern: A highly syncopated, driving 16th-note arpeggio that outlines the chord changes. The pattern evolves in intensity and register throughout the track.
tracks.description: The main melodic and rhythmic element. It enters after the pads and immediately grabs attention with its aggressive, distorted, and resonant tone. It becomes more layered and frantic as the song progresses.

interpretation.score_draft: SPECULATIVE STARTER: Set tempo to 117 BPM. The core is two parts in C minor. PART 1 (Pads): Use a PolySynth with a 'fatsawtooth' oscillator (count: 5, spread: 30), a slow attack (~0.3s) and long release (~1.5s). Add chorus (0.5) and reverb (0.6). Program sustained chords like ['C3', 'Eb3', 'G3']. PART 2 (Lead): Use an FMSynth with harmonicity: 2, modulationIndex: 8 for a metallic tone. Add heavy drive (~0.7) and a resonant lowpass filter (freq: 4500, Q: 4.5). The envelope should be plucky (attack: 0.01, decay: 0.3, sustain: 0.05). Sequence a syncopated 16th-note pattern like ['G4', null, null, 'G4', null, 'Eb4', null, null, 'G4', null, null, 'G4', null, 'Eb4', null, 'C4'].

interpretation.summary: An aggressive, driving monophonic synth bass line that serves as the rhythmic and harmonic core of the track. Its defining characteristic is a gritty, distorted sawtooth waveform shaped by a highly resonant low-pass filter with a plucky envelope, creating a relentless 16th-note motor rhythm that propels the song forward. The sound's intensity varies dramatically through automation of the filter's cutoff frequency.

vocabulary.timbre: A gritty, overdriven monophonic analog-style synthesizer. The core sound is harmonically rich, like a sawtooth wave, with significant distortion. A resonant filter sweep on each note is the dominant timbral feature.
vocabulary.brightness: Highly dynamic. The sound constantly shifts from dark and muted (when the resonant filter is closed down) to bright and buzzy (when the filter opens up). The mean brightness of 474 Hz indicates a bass with strong low-mid frequency content.
vocabulary.envelope: Extremely plucky and percussive. A very fast attack, a quick decay, and zero sustain, coupled with a similar filter envelope, gives each note a sharp, distinct "wow" or "thwack" quality. The release is short, keeping the notes tight.
vocabulary.register_density: The part occupies the low to low-mid register, generally between C2 and C4. It's very dense, playing a nearly continuous stream of 16th notes that form a driving ostinato throughout the entire piece.
vocabulary.harmony_mode: The bassline firmly establishes a C minor tonality. It uses arpeggiated figures and ostinatos that outline the chord progression, drawing notes from the C natural minor scale. It heavily emphasizes the tonic (C) and dominant (G).
vocabulary.groove: A relentless, machine-like 16th-note motor rhythm provides the track's primary propulsive force. While fundamentally straight, the accenting created by the filter envelope and dynamic changes between sections gives it a powerful, driving feel.
vocabulary.space_grit: The sound is defined by its grit, with heavy saturation or distortion applied to the synth. It is presented very dry and direct, with almost no reverb or spatial effects, making it feel immediate, tight, and focused in the mix.

tracks.name: Reso Drive Bass
tracks.pattern: A continuous 16th-note ostinato, arpeggiating notes from the C minor scale. The pattern evolves in 2- or 4-bar phrases, with filter cutoff automation creating large dynamic shifts between sections.
tracks.description: The sole instrument in this stem, this bassline is the track's engine. It enters at the beginning and plays continuously, providing the rhythm, harmony, and core melodic motif. Its intensity is modulated via the filter, creating quiet, tense verses and loud, aggressive choruses.

interpretation.score_draft: SPECULATIVE STARTER: The sound is achievable with a Tone.MonoSynth. The key is the interaction between the envelopes and a resonant filter. Use a 'sawtooth' oscillator and apply significant distortion via `drive: 0.7`. The main envelope should be very plucky: `{ attack: 0.01, decay: 0.2, sustain: 0, release: 0.1 }`. Crucially, set the filter to 'lowpass' with high resonance, `filter.Q.value = 6`. The filter envelope is just as important: `{ attack: 0.005, decay: 0.1, sustain: 0, release: 0.2, baseFrequency: 200, octaves: 3 }`. This creates the sharp 'wow' on each note. The main rhythmic pattern is a constant 16th-note sequence, like `['C2', 'G2', 'C3', 'G2', ...]`. Automate the `filter.frequency` or `filterEnvelope.baseFrequency` to create the dynamic shifts between song sections.

overview.summary: An iconic synth-pop track characterized by a rigid, driving 88 BPM groove, layered synthetic textures, and a melancholic C minor harmony. The arrangement is built around the interplay of a low, pulsing 16th-note bassline and a higher, melodic arpeggio, supported by a classic electronic drum pattern. The track builds dynamically, introducing sustained pads and textural layers to heighten its emotional intensity.

vocabulary.timbre: Dominated by synthetic sources, primarily square and sawtooth waves with noticeable grit and saturation. Percussion is electronic and punchy. Vocals (not modeled) are clear but processed.
vocabulary.brightness: Moderately bright, with a clear separation between the deep bass and the shimmering high-frequency synth lead and hi-hats. The spectral centroid at 2866 Hz reflects the prominence of mid-to-high frequency content.
vocabulary.envelope: Primarily short and percussive envelopes for the main synth lines, creating a tight, staccato, and robotic feel. Plucky bass and lead sounds have sharp attacks and quick decays. Pads introduced later have much slower attacks and longer releases.
vocabulary.register_density: Starts sparse with bass, lead, and drums, creating a wide-open texture. Density increases significantly in chorus sections with the addition of sustained pads and more active vocal layers, filling out the mid-range.
vocabulary.harmony_mode: Firmly in C minor, following a classic pop progression (i-VI-III-VII, or Cm-Ab-Eb-Bb). Harmony is explicitly outlined by the bass root notes and the lead arpeggios.
vocabulary.groove: A relentless and strictly quantized 16th-note pulse defines the groove, driven by the bass and arpeggio synths. The drum pattern is a steady, slightly syncopated anchor.
vocabulary.space_grit: The production is relatively dry and upfront, with minimal reverb on the primary elements. Grit is a key timbral component, achieved through distortion/drive on the bass and lead synths, giving them a warm but aggressive character.

tracks.name: Synth Kick
tracks.pattern: Syncopated four-on-the-floor pattern with an extra hit before beat 4.
tracks.description: The foundational kick drum, providing a powerful and steady pulse throughout the entire track. Its punchy sound cuts through the mix.

tracks.name: Noise Snare
tracks.pattern: A simple backbeat on 2 and 4.
tracks.description: A sharp, synthetic snare that defines the backbeat. Its short, high-frequency burst reinforces the rigid groove.

tracks.name: Metallic Hat
tracks.pattern: Continuous 16th notes.
tracks.description: A constant 16th-note hi-hat pattern that provides the main high-frequency energy and drives the tempo forward. It's present for most of the track.

tracks.name: Pulsing Bass
tracks.pattern: Driving, repeating 16th notes that change pitch with the chord progression (i-VI-III-VII).
tracks.description: The harmonic and rhythmic foundation of the track. This gritty, distorted bass synth plays a relentless 16th-note pattern on the root of each chord, creating a powerful sense of motion. It enters at the very beginning and is nearly always present.

tracks.name: Arpeggio Lead
tracks.pattern: A melodic 16th-note arpeggio outlining the chord progression in a higher register.
tracks.description: The main melodic hook of the song. This brighter synth lead plays a fast, catchy arpeggio that sits on top of the bassline. Its 'fatsaw' sound with some detuning provides width. It enters after the intro and is a defining element.

tracks.name: Chorus Pad
tracks.pattern: Sustained chords that follow the main i-VI-III-VII progression, one chord per measure.
tracks.description: A thick, wide pad that enters during the chorus sections (e.g., around 0:44). It provides a warm harmonic bed under the vocals and arpeggios, with a slow attack and long release that swells and sustains, adding emotional weight.
